title: Break more attack paths with Tenable One Adversary View
summary: With Claude Mythos, Tenable Hexa AI reads scan data like an attacker for vulnerability chains. Adversary View ranks fixes by attack paths stopped.
body_markdown:
Tenable One Adversary View is now generally available. Powered by Claude Mythos, it reads your scan data like an attacker would and tells you what to fix first.


## **Key takeaways**


1. **Adversary View is generally available.** Tenable One customers with Tenable Hexa AI can run it today, with nothing new to deploy.
2. **Tenable Hexa AI applies Claude Mythos’ adversarial reasoning to data you already collect.** It works across the findings from your existing scans and plugins to find vulnerability chains and attack-path choke points.
3. **Break more** **attack paths with fewer fixes.** Adversary View ranks every fix by how many attack paths it stops, so your team can prioritize actions that cut off the most attacker progress.


Virtually every security team works from the same question: What can we fix next to reduce the most risk? Tenable One is designed to answer this question every day with[attack path analysis](https://www.tenable.com/blog/not-a-blackbelt-in-attack-path-analysis-tenable-exposureai-helps-you-achieve-proactive) , which uses rule-based logic to continuously map how attackers could reach your critical assets.


[Tenable One Adversary View](https://www.tenable.com/blog/tenable-one-claude-mythos-5-adversary-view-ai-exposure-management) , now live for all[Tenable Hexa AI](https://www.tenable.com/products/tenable-one/capabilities/hexa-ai) users, adds a deeper, point-in-time check on top of it. Tenable Hexa AI uses Claude’s Mythos-class model to reason like an adversary across your existing scan data, working through how findings combine instead of matching them to predefined rules. Then it points you to the fixes that cut off the most routes.


When Tenable[previewed](https://www.tenable.com/blog/tenable-one-claude-mythos-5-adversary-view-ai-exposure-management) Adversary View[in September,](https://www.tenable.com/blog/tenable-one-claude-mythos-5-adversary-view-ai-exposure-management) we promised a way to see your environment the way an attacker does. If you’re a Tenable One customer with Tenable Hexa AI, you can run it today.


## **Vulnerability management programs must adapt to AI-accelerated discovery**


AI is reshaping[vulnerability management](https://www.tenable.com/solutions/vulnerability-management) by accelerating[vulnerability discovery](https://www.tenable.com/blog/why-the-approaching-flood-of-vulnerabilities-changes-everything-and-what-to-do-about-it) and the creation of working exploits.


For security teams, every new CVE makes it harder to answer the question: “What do we fix next?” These teams still need to understand whether a new CVE applies to their environment, whether they can validate it, and whether anyone is exploiting it. Only then can they start to prioritize it against the thousands of other vulnerabilities across their environment.


But an attacker doesn’t start with a CVSS-sorted spreadsheet of your vulnerabilities. Attackers read the environment to determine which hosts talk to each other, what services are exposed, and which accounts are reachable. Then they reason about how to get from an entry point to a valuable asset.


Severity-based prioritization doesn’t operate that way. A netstat entry, a mapped network drive, or a line buried in plugin output may not be a critical finding on its own, but together they can form a dangerous attack path.


Spotting those combinations across every vulnerability, at this volume, is more than any team can do by hand. Keeping up requires automated attack path analysis, assisted by frontier AI, for prioritization and remediation.


## **What Adversary View does**


Adversary View, accessible in Tenable Hexa AI, looks at your assets from an attacker’s viewpoint. Point Adversary View at a set of assets you already scan and ask how an attacker could move through them.


Tenable Hexa AI uses Claude Mythos to apply adversarial reasoning, building an on-demand graph of your environment from your existing vulnerability scan data, with no new sensors or agents needed, and returns:


- **Ranked vulnerability chains** , with each hop backed by scan evidence
- **Choke points** , and a prioritized list of what to fix, ordered by how many paths each fix closes rather than by severity alone
- **Remediation and reporting includes patches and configuration changes for each route, plus a Jira ticket, remediation dashboard, or shareable PDF report**


Attack path analysis and Adversary View cover different jobs. Attack path analysis watches your environment continuously and flags paths based on pre-defined rules as they form.


> Adversary View is the on-demand deep read: Scope it to a business unit or a tag, and Tenable Hexa AI reasons through that slice of your environment the way an attacker would.


## **Adversary View in action**


We ran Adversary View across a production environment of hosts, and it found and prioritized numerous paths to a crown-jewel asset. The top-ranked path starts at an internet-facing host, moves through a workstation and a domain controller, and ends at a Windows Server 2016 box still vulnerable to EternalBlue, the exploit behind WannaCry.


Adversary View also found a short list of fixes that closes nearly all of the paths: patch two servers (a domain controller and a second Windows Server 2022 box) and you block Server Message Block (SMB) traffic from the internet into the internal network. That one firewall rule closes 32 SMB connections that offer a direct path from the internet into the internal network.


Adversary View is a capability within Tenable One that analyzes existing scan data to identify viable vulnerability chains and the specific routes an attacker could take through connected assets. It is accessed through Tenable Hexa AI and operates as a point-in-time inspection. To begin, the user opens Tenable Hexa AI and selects the Adversary View card. This triggers the agent to analyze scan data and construct a graph of asset connections. The scope can be set to all assets or narrowed to specific tags, IP ranges, or business units. Once submitted, Tenable Hexa AI offers to tag the scoped asset group for future reference. After confirming your scoped assets, Adversary View deterministically builds a map and applies reasoning to discover vulnerability chains without relying on predefined rules. The model interrogates the asset graph step-by-step to identify paths an attacker could traverse. The output includes an executive summary that identifies structural chokepoints and the fixes that are aimed at reducing the most risk. In the example shown, Tenable Hexa AI identified and ranked seven viable attack routes reaching crown-jewel assets. The top-ranked route traces an attacker’s movement from an internet-facing workstation to an EternalBlue-vulnerable server. Each step in a route is backed by actual scan output, including active network connections (NETSTAT_CONN) and specific CVEs, grounding findings in real data. A “What to Fix” section provides tailored remediation recommendations for each route, specifying control changes that disrupt the attacker path across multiple hops. Users can interact with Tenable Hexa AI through follow-up prompts to prioritize fixes and assess risk reduction before applying patches. Tenable Hexa AI is designed to surface the top highest-leverage actions that eliminate maximum exposure. From the conversation, users can create a Jira ticket or Exposure Response initiative directly, with Tenable Hexa AI collecting the technical details needed and allowing the user to define scope before pushing findings into the IT Service Management (ITSM) console.


## **How to run Adversary View in your environment**


Here’s how to run the same analysis on your own assets.


1. **Start a conversation.** Open Tenable Hexa AI and click the “Adversary View” tile, or ask for an Adversary View in your own words.
2. **Set your scope.** The demo uses the “All Assets” option. In your own environment, you can target tags, IP ranges, operating systems, or a business unit. Tenable Hexa AI offers to tag the scoped assets so you can rerun the same analysis later.
3. **Confirm and let it run.** Click “Confirm”. Tenable Hexa AI builds a map of how your scoped assets connect, then uses Claude Mythos to reason across that map and the raw scan evidence behind it. The analysis takes several minutes and keeps running in the background if you leave the panel.
4. **Read the summary.** Results open with an executive summary that includes the top vulnerability chains in your environment and the fixes designed to stop them.
5. **Inspect a route.** Each ranked route shows its hops on a graph, with the scan evidence behind every hop, from SMB sessions and netstat connections to specific CVEs.
6. **Find the fixes that** **matter most.** Each route lists patches and configuration changes that help to stop attacks. Ask Tenable Hexa AI follow-up questions to see which fixes close the most routes at once.
7. **Turn it into tracked work.** Ask Tenable Hexa AI to open a Jira ticket or track your remediation efforts by creating a dashboard. It gathers the technical details, then pushes them into your IT Service Management (ITSM) console.
8. **Generate a report.** Have Tenable Hexa AI generate a PDF and download it straight from the chat. The report summarizes all findings and top actions so you can share results across teams.


### **Prompts to try**


- *Show me an adversary view for assets tagged “production”.*
- *Show me the shortest path from any public entry point to a Critical ACR asset.*
- *Show me the top 3 choke points and explain why each ranks where it does.*
- *If I could only patch 5 assets this sprint, which ones should I pick to close the most vulnerability chains?*


### **Prompts to follow up with**


- *Create JIRA tickets with the top fix and assign them to respective owners.*
- *Ensure MacOS assets are in the appropriate Smart Group to ensure remediation of \[CHOKE POINT\] in the next patching window.*
- *Create a downloadable PDF for all discovered vulnerability chains.*


## **How to get started with Adversary View**


Before your first run, check that you have:


- A **Tenable One Foundation** or **Tenable One Advanced** license
- **“Frontier AI Model Access”** turned on in Tenable Hexa AI’s settings by your admin
- A role with access: Adversary View is on by default for administrators and scan managers, and custom roles need the right permissions
- Scans covering your target assets with the options “ **Override normal verbosity”** enabled and “ **Report as much information as possible”** selected
